question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0019's first-declaration authority, bounded tool-policy tightening, and immutable layered-config snapshot as the permanent V1 contract, with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107026 required to match it exactly?
rationale: The proposal intentionally defines precedence, mutation, and policy-tightening behavior affecting compatibility and security boundaries; tests can validate an implementation but cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Keep Draft Pending Sign-Off
options.body: Require configuration and security-owner approval plus a clause-by-clause parity check against the linked implementation before changing the RFC to accepted.

options.title: Accept V1 Contract
options.body: Approve the current semantics, create the implementation issue, update the metadata to accepted, and proceed with coordinated landing.

options.title: Revise Or Decline Core Seam
options.body: Keep host-side composition or revise precedence and mutation semantics before any core implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Keep Draft Pending Sign-Off
recommendation.body: Require configuration and security-owner approval plus a clause-by-clause parity check against the linked implementation before changing the RFC to accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent configuration history and explicit PR routing make this person the strongest available owner for the cross-cutting product and security-boundary decision.
